instructions.task: Tag the persuader's final message (after 'Persuader message to tag:') with the one persuasion strategy or dialogue act it mainly uses. The dialogue so far is context only.
guidance: Judge only the tagged message; use the context to understand what it replies to.
Statistics about children's suffering are emotion-appeal; facts about the charity itself are credibility-appeal.
If a donation request is combined with a strong reasoning or emotional appeal, choose the appeal.
Short replies: agreement/understanding = acknowledgement; praise of the persuadee's decision or character = praise-user; plain answers, confirmations and closings = other.

Many persuader messages are conversational replies. Tag a persuasion strategy only when the message itself advances a persuasive point; a reply to the persuadee's question or a reaction to their remark is 'other', even if it mentions children, the charity or the persuader's own giving.

If the tagged message is a short fragment that continues the persuader's own previous message (e.g. 'Not at all!' right after 'A dollar you'd never miss.'), label it as that continued message would be labelled.

criteria.greeting: Opening pleasantries: hello, hi, how are you, nice to meet you, or replying to 'how are you' ('I'm good, how are you?').
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of Save the Children, or what they know / want to know about the organization.
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Asks the persuadee's opinions, habits or experience about donating, charities or helping children (e.g. 'Do you donate to charities?', 'Do you believe children in need deserve help?', 'What do you think?'), without directly asking them to donate.
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's personal life unrelated to donation (e.g. 'Do you have children?', 'Where are you from?').
criteria.credibility-appeal: States facts about Save the Children itself: what it is, what it does and where, its history, founder, reputation, ratings, trustworthiness, how funds are spent. Also sharing the charity's website or a link to it, or pointing the persuadee to it for more information. Includes short answers to the persuadee's questions about the charity when they state a fact or vouch for it (e.g. when asked how old it is: 'Over 90 years!'; when asked which charity: 'I really like Save the Children.').
criteria.emotion-appeal: Describes children's suffering or need, including sad statistics about deaths, violence, hunger, or evokes sadness, guilt, sympathy or hope ('The children need your help', 'It breaks my heart'). Must be the persuader actively making a point about children's plight to move the persuadee, not a passing reaction to what the persuadee said. Stating a principle or duty to give ('we should all pitch in') is logical-appeal.
criteria.logical-appeal: Reasons about why donating makes sense or how a donation helps: impact of donations, 'your donation will make a difference', 'even a small donation makes a big difference', 'they can only help when people donate', arithmetic arguments. Also stating a principle or duty about giving: that we should all help, that those who have enough should give, that we must do what we can, or that the persuader couldn't live with themselves if they didn't help.
criteria.personal-story: Tells a narrative about a specific person's experience: the persuader's own experience (e.g. working in Africa, seeing poverty) or a beneficiary's story (e.g. a child helped by the charity).
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader says they themselves donate, will donate or match, or support the charity, as an example to follow ('I donate to them regularly', 'I will also give today').
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Makes an actual request for a small amount, or nudges toward a small first step ('could you afford fifteen cents?', 'May I suggest $.50?', 'Donate just a little'). Also framing the ask as tiny or painless: 'it's only what you'd spend on a coffee or snack', 'just pocket change', 'a dollar you won't even miss'.
criteria.donation-information: Explains how the donation in this task works: amount range ($0 to the full payment), deducted from the task payment, the research team collects and sends it, asking people to give part of their payment, how to donate.
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Directly asks or urges the persuadee to donate, without naming an amount ('Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?', 'We should donate to them!', 'Would you donate then?').
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asks how much the persuadee will or would like to donate.
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee (for their time, donation, chat). Includes thanking on the children's behalf after the persuadee agrees to give ('The kids will be so grateful for it').
criteria.praise-user: Compliments the persuadee's generosity, kindness or decision to donate ('That's awesome and generous!', 'You are very kind', 'People like you make the world better', 'Great!' right after the persuadee agrees to donate). Not for reacting to an ordinary remark or idea.
criteria.acknowledgement: Signals agreement or understanding of what the persuadee said: 'Ok, I understand', 'I agree', 'Me too', 'Yeah I know', 'Absolutely.', 'This is true', 'That makes sense'. Also agreeing with or echoing a positive remark the persuadee made (e.g. persuadee: 'they do good work' -> persuader: 'They sure do, truly a blessing').
criteria.off-task: Chat unrelated to the charity or donation: small talk about places, weather, the HIT or survey mechanics, jokes.
criteria.other_answer: Answers or replies to a question or comment the persuadee just made, conversationally, e.g. about the persuader's own habits or life ('No, I just give when I can', 'yes, it keeps me busy' when asked about volunteering), or plain yes/no replies ('Yes, they are.', 'I'm not sure of the details'). If the answer states facts about the charity (its age, work, ratings), it is credibility-appeal instead.
criteria.other_confirm: Confirms or checks the amount or decision the persuadee chose ('So you are donating $10, right?'), or asks payment logistics like one-time vs monthly.
criteria.other_closing: Closing remarks, goodbyes, well-wishes ('Have a great day!'), 'you're welcome'.
criteria.other_react: Reacts to or comments on what the persuadee just said ('That sounds like fun!', 'That is too bad', 'That's great to hear', 'Isn't that amazing?') without itself making a new persuasive point.
criteria.other_misc: Any other filler or generic remark that fits none of the categories above (e.g. a generic 'Isn't that amazing?', 'That's great to hear' not praising the persuadee).
